name: Battle of Mikatagahara

phases.title: The armies take their ground on the plain
phases.text: Ieyasu drew up his forces in a line on the plain of Mikatagahara. Shingen arrayed his men in the fish-scale formation in four lines, with the vanguard first and Baba Nobuharu in the fourth.

phases.title: The Takeda cavalry overruns the Tokugawa right
phases.text: As snow began to fall the Tokugawa arquebusiers opened fire. Naitō Masatoyo's vanguard cavalry attacked all the same and overran Honda Tadakatsu's segment on the Tokugawa right.

phases.title: The Oda force is routed and the rear is charged
phases.text: The Takeda horsemen turned on the Oda reinforcements, who were quickly overrun and routed, and then charged the Tokugawa rear.

phases.title: A second Takeda attack breaks the line
phases.text: Shingen withdrew his vanguard to rest and sent fresh horsemen under Katsuyori in a two-pronged charge, closely followed by the main body. Their weight drove the Tokugawa army into a disorderly retreat.

phases.title: Ieyasu flees and his units are overrun
phases.text: Ieyasu left the field, and several of his retainers died as their units were encircled and overrun. The Takeda vanguard under Baba Nobuharu and Yamagata Masakage came on and stopped short of Hamamatsu to make camp for the night.

phases.title: A night raid and the Takeda withdrawal
phases.text: A small band of Tokugawa foot soldiers and gunners attacked the Takeda camp and threw the vanguard into confusion. Shingen, uncertain of the Tokugawa strength, decided to withdraw to his own territories.

note: The Takeda order of battle (four lines in the fish-scale formation) is the one given in the Kōyō Gunkan, a Takeda family record. The accounts do not give the Tokugawa formations' exact places beyond a line with Honda Tadakatsu's segment on the right, a left and a centre, and the Oda reinforcements alongside. The Oda force is placed at the right rear and the arquebusiers in front of the line by judgement. The plain lay just north of Hamamatsu; the Takeda are drawn at the top and the spacing of their lines is schematic. The first and second Takeda lines are drawn as one cavalry body.
